applicationType.question: Are you applying for SNAP for the first time, or renewing?
applicationType.explanation: Renewing (recertifying) means you already get SNAP and your certification period is ending
applicationType.example: If you have never had SNAP, or your SNAP stopped, choose applying

noticeLanguage.question: What language do you want your letters from SNAP in?
noticeLanguage.explanation: SNAP will mail you letters about your case

altFormat.question: Are you blind or seriously visually impaired and want your letters in another format?
altFormat.explanation: Braille is available if none of the other formats work for you

phone.question: What is your phone number?
phone.explanation: SNAP interviews are usually done by phone

otherPhone.question: Is there another phone number where you can be reached?
otherPhone.example: A work phone or a family member's phone

primaryAddress.question: What is your home address?
primaryAddress.explanation: Use the address where you live now, even if it is temporary
primaryAddress.skipLabel: I don't have a permanent address

mailingAddress.question: Where should SNAP mail your letters?
mailingAddress.explanation: Only fill this in if it is different from your home address
mailingAddress.example: A P.O. box or a friend's address

firstName.question: What is {name}'s first name?
firstName.explanation: Use the legal name on their ID or Social Security card

lastName.question: What is {name}'s last name?
lastName.explanation: Use the legal name on their ID or Social Security card

relationship.question: How is {name} related to you?
relationship.explanation: List everyone who lives with you, even if they are not applying

buysAndPrepares.question: Do you buy and make food together with {name}?
buysAndPrepares.explanation: People who buy and cook food together count as one SNAP household. Spouses and children under 22 who live with their parents always count together
buysAndPrepares.example: If you share groceries and meals with your roommate, answer yes. If you each buy your own food, answer no

isApplying.question: Is {name} applying for SNAP?
isApplying.explanation: You can apply for some people in your household and not others. For example, parents who can't get SNAP because of immigration status can still apply for their children

sex.question: What is {name}'s sex?
sex.explanation: Choose what is on their ID if you are not sure

ssn.question: What is {name}'s Social Security number?
ssn.explanation: Everyone applying for SNAP needs one. If they don't have one, they can still apply and will be asked to apply for a number

otherNames.question: Has {name} ever used any other names?
otherNames.explanation: Include maiden names or names from a previous marriage

citizenStatus.question: Is {name} a U.S. citizen?
citizenStatus.explanation: Many non-citizens can get SNAP too. Your answer does not affect anyone's immigration case

options.label: Yes, U.S. citizen or U.S. national
No, citizen of Micronesia, the Marshall Islands or Palau

isHispanic.question: Is {name} Hispanic or Latino?
isHispanic.explanation: This is optional and does not affect eligibility or benefits

race.question: What is {name}'s race? Choose all that apply
race.explanation: This is optional and does not affect eligibility or benefits

educationLevel.questionSelf: What is the highest level of school you have finished?
educationLevel.question: What is the highest level of school {name} has finished?
educationLevel.explanation: This is optional and does not affect eligibility or benefits

options.label: Less than high school diploma or equivalency

highestGrade.questionSelf: What is the highest grade you have completed?
highestGrade.question: What is the highest grade {name} has completed?
highestGrade.explanation: If they are in high school now, use the last grade they finished
highestGrade.example: If they are in 10th grade, answer 9

primaryLanguage.questionSelf: What language do you speak most often?
primaryLanguage.question: What language does {name} speak most often?
primaryLanguage.explanation: This is optional and does not affect eligibility or benefits

disabilityBenefits.question: Does {name} get disability benefits?
disabilityBenefits.explanation: For example SSI, Social Security Disability (SSDI), veterans disability, or New York State disability

hasMedicalBills.question: Does {name} have medical bills?
hasMedicalBills.explanation: These can lower how much income SNAP counts for people who are 60 or older or have a disability
hasMedicalBills.example: Doctor or dental visits, prescriptions, health insurance, eyeglasses, hearing aids, rides to medical appointments

medicalBillsDetails.question: What are {name}'s medical bills for, how much are they, and who pays them?
medicalBillsDetails.example: Prescriptions, $40 a month, paid by me

hasSpenddown.question: Is {name} on Medicaid with a spenddown?
hasSpenddown.explanation: A spenddown means you have to pay some medical costs yourself each month before Medicaid pays

inSchoolTeen.question: Is {name} enrolled in school or a training program?

isStudent.question: Is {name} enrolled at least half-time in college or a trade school?
isStudent.explanation: This means a college or university, or a business, technical, trade or vocational school that requires a high school diploma or equivalency. Not high school. Half-time is set by the school, usually about 6 credits a semester. Students enrolled less than half-time should answer no
isStudent.example: If they take 9 credits at a community college, answer yes. If they take one 3-credit class, answer no

schoolName.question: What is the name of {name}'s school or training program?

schoolFullTime.question: Is {name} a full-time student?
schoolFullTime.explanation: Check with the school if you are not sure
schoolFullTime.example: If they take 12 credits this semester, answer yes

schoolIncome.question: Does {name} get any money from school?

studentExemption.question: Does any of these describe {name}?
studentExemption.explanation: College students can get SNAP if at least one of these is true: has a paid job for at least 20 hours a week (self-employed counts if they earn at least minimum wage for those hours); is approved for a work-study job this school term and expects to work; is in an on-the-job training program; takes care of someone in the household under 6; takes care of someone in the household age 6 to 11 and can't get child care to go to class and work; is a single parent studying full-time who takes care of a child under 12; gets cash assistance (Temporary Assistance); was placed in school by a job training program such as SNAP Employment and Training, WIOA or the Trade Act; or is physically or mentally unable to work
studentExemption.example: If they work 22 hours a week at a store, or their financial aid includes a work-study job they'll be working this semester, answer yes

fosterCareAt18.questionSelf: Were you in foster care on your 18th birthday?
fosterCareAt18.question: Was {name} in foster care on their 18th birthday?

boarderOrFoster.question: Is {name} a boarder, foster child or foster adult?
boarderOrFoster.explanation: A boarder pays you for a room and meals

anyonePregnant.question: Is anyone in your household age 16 or older pregnant?
anyonePregnant.explanation: Choose everyone who is pregnant, including yourself

anyoneWorkLimited.question: Does anyone in your household age 16 or older have a medical condition that limits how much or what kind of work they can do?
anyoneWorkLimited.explanation: This can be physical or mental. Choose everyone it applies to, including yourself
anyoneWorkLimited.example: A back injury that means they can't lift heavy things

livesInNewYork.question: Do you live in New York State?
livesInNewYork.explanation: You have to live in New York to get New York SNAP

snapElsewhere.question: Is anyone in your household applying for or getting SNAP or cash assistance somewhere else?
snapElsewhere.explanation: For example, in another state or another county

treatmentOrGroupHome.question: Does anyone in your household live in a drug or alcohol treatment center or a state-certified group home or supported apartment?

hasIncome.question: Does anyone in your household get any income?
hasIncome.explanation: Income includes wages, self-employment, child support, Social Security or SSI, unemployment, pensions, veterans benefits, and money from friends or family

hasMoreIncome.question: Does anyone in your household get income that isn't on the documents you uploaded?
hasMoreIncome.explanation: Income includes wages, self-employment, child support, Social Security or SSI, unemployment, pensions, veterans benefits, and money from friends or family
hasMoreIncome.example: If you uploaded your pay stub but your partner also works, answer yes

incomeType.question: What kind of income is this?

options.label: Rent from a roomer or boarder
Other (including money from friends or family)

incomeSource.question: Who pays this income?
incomeSource.explanation: The employer, agency or person the money comes from

incomeAmount.question: How much is each payment, before taxes and deductions?
incomeAmount.explanation: Use the gross amount. For self-employment, use what you earn minus what it costs you to do the work
incomeAmount.example: If your pay stub says gross pay $650, answer 650

incomeFrequency.question: How often is it paid?
incomeFrequency.example: If you get paid every other Friday, choose every two weeks

incomeHours.question: About how many hours a month is this work?
incomeHours.explanation: Use your average if your hours change
incomeHours.example: If you work about 20 hours a week, answer 87

incomeChanged.question: In the last 30 days, has anyone in your household changed or quit a job, or had their hours or income cut?

pendingIncome.question: Is anyone in your household expecting income they haven't received yet?
pendingIncome.example: A new job that hasn't paid yet, or an unemployment claim that is still being processed

pendingIncomeDetails.question: Tell us about the income you're expecting
pendingIncomeDetails.explanation: Who it's for, where it's from, and about how much
pendingIncomeDetails.example: My first paycheck from my new job at Target, about $500, on the 15th

onStrike.question: Is anyone in your household on strike?

dependentCareMonthly.question: How much does your household pay each month for child care or adult dependent care so someone can work, look for work, or go to school or training?
dependentCareMonthly.explanation: Enter 0 if you don't pay for care. This cost can lower how much income SNAP counts
dependentCareMonthly.example: If you pay a babysitter $50 a week while you work, answer 217

hasCashOrAccounts.question: Does anyone in your household have cash or money in a bank account that isn't on a statement you uploaded?
hasCashOrAccounts.explanation: Include cash at home, checking and savings accounts, and accounts shared with someone outside your household. This only affects how fast you can get SNAP

hasFinancialAssets.question: Does anyone in your household have other savings or investments?
hasFinancialAssets.example: Stocks, bonds, savings bonds, retirement accounts, IRAs, mutual funds, trust funds, CDs

hasVehicles.question: Does anyone in your household have a car, truck or other vehicle?

assetMember.question: Who does this belong to?
assetMember.explanation: If it's shared, choose the person in your household it belongs to

assetAmount.question: About how much is it worth?
assetAmount.explanation: For a bank account, use the current balance

vehicleMakeModel.question: What make and model is the vehicle?

ownsProperty.question: Does anyone applying own any property, including your home?
ownsProperty.explanation: Buildings, land, rental property, or a vacation home

propertyDetails.question: What property, and who owns it?
propertyDetails.example: Our house at 123 Main St, owned by me and my wife

propertyTransferred.question: In the last 3 months, has anyone applying sold, given away or transferred cash or property to qualify for SNAP?

livingSituation.question: Which of these describe where you live? Choose all that apply

options.label: I own my home or am paying a mortgage
I live with relatives or friends
I don't have a permanent place to live
I'm a migrant or seasonal farmworker

rentOrMortgage.question: How much do you pay for rent or mortgage each month?
rentOrMortgage.explanation: Include only your household's share if you split costs with people outside your household
rentOrMortgage.example: If your rent is $1,200 and you split it evenly with a roommate who buys their own food, answer 600

propertyTax.question: How much property tax do you pay on your home each year?
propertyTax.explanation: Enter 0 if it's included in your mortgage payment

homeInsurance.question: How much do you pay for homeowner's insurance each year?
homeInsurance.explanation: Enter 0 if it's included in your mortgage payment

paysHeat.question: Do you pay for heat separately from your rent or mortgage?
paysHeat.example: If you get a gas bill for your heat, answer yes. If heat is included in your rent, answer no

heatType.question: What kind of heat do you have?

heatCompany.question: What company do you pay for heat?

heatAccount.question: What is your heating account number?

paysAirConditioning.question: Do you pay for air conditioning, either in your electric bill or as a separate fee?
paysAirConditioning.example: If you use an air conditioner and pay your own electric bill, answer yes

paysOtherUtilities.question: Do you pay separately for any other utilities?
paysOtherUtilities.explanation: For example electricity, cooking gas, water, trash, or a fee to set up utilities
paysOtherUtilities.example: If you pay your own electric bill, answer yes

someoneElsePays.question: Does anyone else pay any of these housing costs for you?
someoneElsePays.explanation: For example Section 8 or another housing program

paysChildSupport.question: Does anyone in your household pay court-ordered child support?
paysChildSupport.explanation: This can lower how much income SNAP counts

childSupportChildren.question: Which children is it paid for?

fleeingFelon.question: Is anyone in your household breaking a condition of probation or parole, or running from a felony charge, and being actively looked for by police?
fleeingFelon.explanation: The law requires us to ask everyone these questions

courtParoleViolation.question: Has a court found that anyone in your household is violating probation or parole?

snapFraud.question: Has anyone in your household ever been disqualified from SNAP for fraud or breaking program rules on purpose?

tradedForWeaponsOrDrugs.question: Since September 22, 1996, has anyone in your household been convicted of trading SNAP benefits for guns, ammunition, explosives or drugs?

soldSnap.question: Since September 22, 1996, has anyone in your household been convicted of buying or selling $500 or more of SNAP benefits?

duplicateSnap.question: Since September 22, 1996, has anyone in your household been convicted of getting SNAP in more than one place at the same time by lying about who they are or where they live?

wantsAuthorizedRep.question: Do you want someone outside your household to be able to apply for you or use an EBT card to buy food for you?
wantsAuthorizedRep.explanation: This is called an authorized representative. It's optional
wantsAuthorizedRep.example: A neighbor who does your grocery shopping

authorizedRepName.question: What is your representative's full name?

authorizedRepPhone.question: What is your representative's phone number?

authorizedRepEbt.question: Should your representative get their own EBT card to buy food for you?

notes.question: Is there anything else you want SNAP to know?
notes.explanation: If you are renewing, tell us what has changed since last time, like a move, a new baby, or someone moving in or out
